subject: Orchard AI — MSA & Order Form: announcement / logo use (redline escalation)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Orchard AI — Order Form / publicity ask (initial capture)

Quick capture — Orchard legal sent back a redlined MSA with a broad publicity carveout they want removed. External asked for: (1) ability to list Orchard as a customer in marketing materials, (2) explicit logo usage in press/website, and (3) a short quote we can use in a launch note. Their redline removes our standard "publicity is opt-out" language and instead demands a case-by-case approval workflow that sits with their procurement team.

Laura / Priyom — can you take their redline (attached) and identify: which bits we can accept without escalation, which require Sales+Legal signoff, and any ask that would materially weaken our go-to-market (e.g., limiting aggregate references, removing logos from product pages)?

Attachments: Orchard_OrderForm_v3.docx (customer redline)

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchard AI — Order Form / publicity ask (initial capture)

Thanks Alex — reading through. High-level notes:

- Their redline changes Section 9 (Publicity) to require "written approval for each use" and inserts a 10-business-day review window. This would make programmatic references impossible and is a blocker for PLG case study cadence.
- They tighten Confidential Information carveout to include "customer-derived prompts and outputs" which is a security/compliance concern for data residency customers.
- They request a separate asset licensing clause that grants them a non-exclusive, perpetual right to use Redwood logos in perpetuity.

I recommend the following approach:
1) Push back on the per-use approval. Offer an opt-in publicity clause: they can opt in during onboarding to allow automated references; otherwise default stays: Redwood may list Orchard as a customer with a 7-day pre-notice for sensitive announcements.
2) Narrow the confidentiality language: keep customer-derived prompts under customer control, but exclude aggregated telemetry (analytics) from Confidential Information with an explicit anonymization requirement.
3) Limit logo rights to "use for the duration of the contract, in marketing materials and website, subject to trademark guidelines" — no perpetual conveyance.

I'll draft suggested redlines and send to Dev/legal. If this escalates beyond a standard concession we should flag for Sales Manager approval (discount/credit tradeoffs).

— Priyom

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-02T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchard AI — Order Form / publicity ask (initial capture)

Priyom — I uploaded a PDF with inline comments (MSA_redline_20251202.pdf). Key legal positions below (summarized):

- Publicity: accept opt-in for automated references (we call it "Marketing Opt-In") where customer can select "Yes" on the Order Form. If they opt-in we can list them and use logo per brand guidelines; if they decline we accept the 7-day pre-notification window on case-by-case press.
- Approval timeline: push back on a rigid 10-business-day approval window. We can agree to a good-faith review and a 5-business-day review for standard requests; material releases get longer review.
- Logo grant: limit to "non-exclusive, revocable license for the term of the agreement" with a requirement to stop use within 30 days post-termination. No perpetual grant.
- Quote/testimonial: require a short sign-off copy and cap aggregated length (30 words) and attribution scope (name, title, company).
- Confidentiality: carve out anonymized, aggregated usage data from Confidential Information, keep customer prompts/outputs as customer-controlled unless customer explicitly allows reuse.

I'll add these as redline markup to the Order Form and MSA. Alex — if they insist on perpetual logo rights or unlimited publicity vetoes escalate to Sales Director; we should consider a commercial concession but not legal.

Attachments: MSA_redline_20251202.pdf
Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@orchardai.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sienna Clarke <sienna@orchardai.com>
Cc: "Laura Bennett" <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, "Priyom Das" <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-02T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — publicity and logo language (Orchard comments)

Hi team — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from Orchard legal: 

1) The concern about per-use approvals is primarily about timing. Our comms team can't commit to a perpetual opt-in because their legal requires explicit sign-off to avoid surprises during product launches. They requested 10 business days as a safe default.
2) Regarding logo use: Orchard is comfortable with a term-limited license but asked for an extension to 90 days after termination to avoid breaking historical collateral during an active close-out period.
3) For the quote/testimonial: they want to provide a product-focused quote (no more than 50 words) but reserve the right to edit attribution if the quoted person leaves the company.

Can you confirm if the 90-day post-termination window is a hard no, or if we can accept 90 days with a clause that Redwood may request an expedited takedown for specific materials?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Ross
Head of Legal, Orchard AI

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@orchardai.com>, Sienna Clarke <sienna@orchardai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-03T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA — publicity and logo language (Orchard comments)

Emily — appreciate the clarity and the middle ground. Quick responses to the three asks: 

1) Approval timeline: we can accept a standard 7-business-day review for non-material requests and 10 business days as a maximum for product launch notices if Orchard needs the extra cushion. We'll commit to a "good faith" expedited path for time-sensitive items and include a dispute resolution step for exceptional holds.

2) Logo post-termination window: Redwood's preference is 30 days. However, we're willing to accept 90 days for legacy collateral ONLY if: (a) Orchard agrees to provide a list of all assets using Redwood's mark within 30 days of termination, and (b) Redwood can require takedown of any live materials posing regulatory or security concerns with 48 hours' notice.

3) Testimonial attribution: 50 words is fine, and we can include a small clause allowing Orchard to request attribution edits for personnel changes. We'll add a simple approval flow for final text.

If that works for Orchard, we'll incorporate the negotiated language into the Order Form and get final sign-off. If they still require perpetual logo rights or unilateral per-use vetoes we'll need to escalate to Sales Director for a commercial concession.

Next steps: Priyom / Dev — can you update the redline to reflect the 7/10 day compromise, a 90-day legacy window with the two safeguards, and the testimonial parameters? I will then send to Sienna/Emily and link the DocuSign packet.

Alex
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: press_excerpt.png (example of proposed logo treatment)
